content.user_title: Add Fingerprint Regression Gates to CI
content.value_statement: Browser fingerprint changes can silently break automated Chromium workflows. This skill adds repeatable liarjs scans, baseline comparisons, and score gates to CI pipelines.
actual_capabilities: Creates version-pinned liarjs commands for fingerprint scans.
Adds minimum-score gates that fail CI below a selected threshold.
Compares current scan results with a committed baseline.
Provides GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Docker, and Playwright patterns.
Configures offline or self-hosted endpoint operation.
Explains scan exit codes and artifact retention.
limitations: Requires Node.js 22 or newer and an available Chromium browser.
Does not install or configure a compatible browser automatically.
Headless and headed scans require separate baselines.
Online mode sends a request to liarjs.dev unless another endpoint is configured.

use_cases.title: Protect Browser Automation Builds
use_cases.description: Add a fingerprint baseline comparison before deploying changes to a Chromium automation harness.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Fingerprint Checks
use_cases.description: Create repeatable score gates and artifacts across GitHub Actions or GitLab CI.

use_cases.title: Verify Test Browser Consistency
use_cases.description: Assert specific fingerprint checks inside an existing Playwright suite.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Score Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a version-pinned liarjs fingerprint check to my GitHub Actions workflow. Use Node.js 22 and fail when the score is below 60.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple CI threshold.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Against a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CI workflow that saves scan.json, compares it with baseline.json, and uploads the current scan after every run.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detect changes from a known browser state.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an Offline Runner
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my fingerprint gate for an air-gapped GitLab runner. Use offline mode and explain which checks are unavailable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep all scan traffic inside a restricted environment.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Playwright Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Add authorized fingerprint assertions to my Playwright suite. Ignore only documented environment-specific checks and prevent unrelated score changes from hiding failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Apply precise checks to an existing browser harness.

output_examples.input: Add a fingerprint gate to a GitHub Actions job.
output: Use Node.js 22 and a version-pinned liarjs dependency.
Run the headless scan with a minimum score of 60.
Upload the scan report even when the gate fails.

output_examples.input: Our datacenter runner always fails the timezone check.
output_examples.output: Use a baseline comparison from the same runner mode. Document the timezone exception instead of lowering the global score threshold.

output_examples.input: Keep fingerprint tests inside our network.
output_examples.output: Use offline mode for JavaScript checks or direct the cross-layer checks to an approved self-hosted endpoint.

best_practices: Pin liarjs with an exact version and a committed lockfile.
Create baselines in the same browser mode and runner environment used by CI.
Store scan artifacts and explain every deliberate baseline change.
anti_patterns: Do not disable the Chromium sandbox to make a container start.
Do not lower a global threshold to hide one environment-specific check.
Do not use fingerprint testing against systems without explicit authorization.

faq.question: What does the CI gate measure?
faq.answer: It measures liarjs browser fingerprint consistency and can compare individual check results with a saved baseline.

faq.question: Which runtime does the skill require?
faq.answer: The examples require Node.js 22 or newer and a discoverable Chrome, Chromium, or Edge browser.

faq.question: Should I use a score floor or a baseline?
faq.answer: Use a baseline when your environment has known permanent failures. Use a score floor for stable, controlled runners.

faq.question: Does the scan make network requests?
faq.answer: Online mode contacts liarjs.dev for cross-layer checks. Offline mode skips those checks, and a self-hosted endpoint is supported.

faq.question: How should I update a baseline?
faq.answer: Refresh it in a dedicated commit and record the observed differences and reason.

faq.question: Can this run inside Playwright?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference shows checkPage assertions against the page and browser configuration already used by the test suite.
